answers.explanation: Everyone has to find the printer, so its address must not change. Servers, printers, routers, and access points are static.
If DHCP hands out an address that's already typed into a printer, both devices break. The ranges must never overlap.
Short-stay networks need short leases (an hour or a few) so addresses come back to the pool quickly.
The first usable address, like 192.168.10.1 in 192.168.10.0/24. Some sites use the last; the point is to pick one rule.
The network address is 10.1.1.64, so the first usable host is 10.1.1.65.
An IPv4 address is always 32 bits. Every bit added to the network part is taken from the host part: robbing Peter to pay Paul.
One more borrowed bit: 4 subnets of 62 hosts become 8 subnets of 30.
The lease time, sometimes called its TTL. Match it to how long devices stay on that subnet.
